title: Blue, red and purple teams: roles and cooperation

videos.script: Every defence in this course so far was tested by the person who built it. That is useful, and it has a blind spot. You test for the attacks you thought of. {{blind}} So organisations borrow an idea from military exercises. One team defends: the blue team. Another plays the attacker, with permission and rules: the red team. {{teams}} When the two work apart, the red team writes a report and the blue team reads it months later. When they sit together, each attack is followed at once by a question. Did we see that? {{purple}} That is purple teaming. In the lab you will run one small exercise. Six wrong passwords from the internet, and a look at what the portal's log made of them. {{lab}} The log saw every attempt. It also turned out to be missing two things a defender needs. {{finding}}
